page.title: Why tinyactors exists
page.description: Why tinyactors exists, who maintains it, its license, where its source is and how it is released.

hero.headline: Model every system as a statechart
hero.lede: tinyactors runs SCXML charts as actors inside programs that already chose their I/O, threads and memory. It is MIT licensed and maintained by _dhamidi at Amp.
hero.author: Dario Hamidi

section.heading: Give stateful logic one home
section.p: The state of a live websocket connection, with its retries, reconnects and timeouts, often has no clear home in a system. An actor models how one connection behaves, without the whole system in your head.
The core does no I/O, starts no threads and allocates no memory itself. So it embeds in a runtime that already decided all three.

claim.statement: The core uses no C library
claim.p: Your program gives it an allocator, performs its effects and tells it the time.

section.heading: Maintained by _dhamidi at Amp
section.p: tinyactors is maintained by _dhamidi at Amp. Its license names Dario Hamidi as the copyright holder.

section.heading: Use it under the MIT license
section.p: You may use, change and ship tinyactors in any program, keeping its copyright and permission notice.

claim.p: The repository's license covers the C core, and the Node.js and Python packages declare MIT too.

section.heading: Read the source and its tests
section.p: One repository holds the C core, the Node.js and Python packages, the conformance suite and this site. Every binding runs the same suite.

section.heading: Follow each release in the changelog
section.p: Each package is released on its own. Its changelog says what changed in each release and how to upgrade.
The API is still changing: the README says breaking changes are made frequently to land on a good API.
